Steph — quick guidance from tax ops (summarized):

1) Presence of an EIN alone does not automatically make an entity a US person for withholding/1099 purposes. We must determine the entity classification under regs (disregarded entity, partnership, corporation) and whether the owner(s) are US persons.

2) If Eastshore is a foreign entity (UK-resident) with a UK parent as beneficial owner, a properly completed W-8BEN-E that documents chapter 3 status and includes UBO info is acceptable. That would limit (usually zero) US withholding but also mean they are not 1099-reportable as a US person.

3) If Eastshore is a US domestic LLC (organized under US state law) or a foreign LLC that has elected US tax classification (i.e., filed to be treated as US person), they must provide a signed W-9 with EIN and certs, and we would treat them as 1099-eligible where payments meet thresholds.

What we need right now to resolve:
- A copy of the Certificate of Formation / Registrar filing showing jurisdiction of formation (US state vs UK).
- Clarification on beneficial owner(s) — is Eastshore Holdings Ltd (UK) the controlling owner? If so, request Chapter 4 FATCA GIIN if applicable.
- If they claim US tax status, we need a signed W-9 with printed name and signature of authorized signatory.

Action: Steph, please ask the vendor (Oliver) to confirm formation jurisdiction and send either the signed W-9 OR a completed, signed W-8BEN-E plus registrar docs showing UK formation and the ownership chain. Also request a bank letter that includes the beneficiary name as matching legal name on W-8/W-9 (they already sent one — please confirm bank letter name).

I can sign off to release payment once we have the registrar doc + appropriate signed tax form. If they insist they are US person despite UK operations, route to legal for confirmation.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Finance & Tax — Redwood Inference
